output.summary: KEP-4412 lets the kubelet send a projected service account token (PSAT), bound to the pod and its service account with a configured audience, to kubelet credential provider plugins via stdin, so image pulls can be tied to workload identity without long-lived secrets. The KEP is marked implementable at stage beta.
output.rationale: Today image pulls rely on long-lived image pull secrets stored in the API or on node-wide kubelet credential providers that any pod on the node can use. The proposal adds an optional tokenAttributes field so a provider can receive a per-pod token and selected service account annotations. Reviewers raised concerns about cache keying, annotation exposure, and downgrade safety, which led to a separate apiserver feature gate that must be beta and enabled one release before this KEP reaches beta.

alternatives.option: Always pass the service account token through to the registry and rely on registry proxies to perform STS exchange
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists this only under Alternatives with no stated reason for rejection, so the sources do not say why it was not chosen.

alternatives.option: Pass arbitrary pod annotations to the credential provider
alternatives.why_not: Reviewer liggitt said this 'makes an effectively unlimited surface area', and the design moved to service account annotations listed explicitly in serviceAccountAnnotationKeys.

alternatives.option: Let the credential provider look up service account info directly from the Kubernetes API
alternatives.why_not: Raised by liggitt as an alternative in review; the sources do not record a final rejection rationale.

evidence.quote: When it is set, the Kubelet will provision a token with the given audience bound to the current pod and its service account.
Removed pod annotations and added a new service account annotations field in the credential provider config to define the annotations that'll be plumbed to the plugin
Added a new feature gate and updated the beta criteria to include what @enj mentioned.
This feature needs to be beta/enabled by default at least one release before this KEP goes to beta. This is critical to support downgrade use cases.
